stem: You partition a long list of independent circuits into several jobs and run them in batch mode. Besides shorter queuing, what practical advantage does this give over submitting everything as one giant job?

options.text: You get each job's results separately, so you can usually cancel the rest early or re-run only the job that failed.
Batch mode reserves the QPU exclusively for the whole run, so no other user's jobs interleave with your batched circuits.
Batch mode applies stronger error mitigation than a single job.
A batch never counts against your usage or cost.

explanation.correct: Partitioning into multiple batched jobs makes results more flexible to work with: you receive each job's result separately, so you can stop early by cancelling remaining jobs, or re-run just a failed job instead of the entire workload.

distractors.B: Batch mode does not give exclusive access — that is a session feature. Batched jobs share the QPU with everyone else's.
distractors.C: Error mitigation is controlled by primitive options, not by the execution mode; batching does not change it.
distractors.D: Batched jobs still consume QPU usage and count against cost; batching does not make execution free.

provenance.notes: meta-pattern fix pass: length/stem-echo/absolute calibration (s4) — trimmed correct A, lengthened exclusivity distractor (length-tell fix). Also: hedge added to the correct option (hedge-heuristic calibration).
